source.title: A Chabauty–Coleman bound for surfaces
readSections: Only the explicitly recorded selections of prerequisite sources were read.
source.versionNote: The fully read v2 predates the 54-page publication; final-source reconciliation is G0. Error findings concern v2 only. Later Balakrishnan–Caro quotes a different constant and domain.

files.name: debarre
files.read: §2 through Theorem 2.1; §3 through Lemma 3.6; beginning of §4

files.name: garcia-fritz

summary: Complete reading of the available preprint, atomic extraction and source-qualified routing for overdetermined jets, abelian differential restriction, formal Lie theory and local surface Chabauty. The false geometric branch bound, printed formal-group construction and canonical-ampleness claim are recorded with counterexamples; numerical global endpoints and unmatched original suppliers remain withheld. Existing suppliers retain their owners; two Part II briefs cover formal Lie theory and surface methods. No formalization is claimed.

items.name: Abelian variety over a field
items.statement: An abelian variety over K is a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K; smoothness and commutativity are derived.
items.note: API: Reuse zero, products, field base change and group homomorphisms; keep the relative abelian-scheme extension separate. Tests: (1) dimension three is allowed; (2) properness is a hypothesis; (3) a field object does not supply an integral model.

items.name: Tangent space at the identity
items.statement: T₀A is the Zariski tangent space at the rational identity, with the K-action transported from its residue field.
items.note: API: Reuse TangentSpace and its residue-field comparison; construct invariant differentials separately. Tests: (1) zero point is K-rational; (2) scalar extension must be identified; (3) finite dimensionality is not a logarithm.

items.name: Finite-dimensional abelian tangent space
items.statement: For an abelian variety A/K, T₀A is finite dimensional over K.

items.name: Algebraic Kähler differentials
items.statement: For commutative R-algebra S, Ω[S/R] represents R-derivations into S-modules.
items.note: API: Reuse D, linearMapEquivDerivation and map for a commutative algebra square; sheafify and supply completion comparisons separately. Tests: (1) d(ab)=a db+b da; (2) d(r)=0 for r in R; (3) ordinary differentials of K[[z]] are not silently continuous.

items.name: One-dimensional formal group law
items.statement: FormalGroup R is a power series in two variables with identity linear part, zero constant term and associativity; commutativity is the separate IsComm property.
items.note: API: Import the one-dimensional carrier; a dimension-n law is a new construction, not Fin n copies of this type. Tests: (1) additive law qualifies; (2) multiplicative law X+Y+XY qualifies; (3) n=3 needs a vector of series in six variables.

items.name: Last maximal coefficient of a restricted series
items.statement: If c>0 and a nonzero power series over a normed ring is restricted at c, some last coefficient attains its Gauss norm and every later weighted norm is strictly smaller.
items.note: This is not the zero-count theorem.

items.name: Multiplicative Gauss norm
items.statement: For restricted power series f,g over an ultrametric normed ring with multiplicative norm and c>0, ||fg||_c=||f||_c ||g||_c.

items.name: Abelian scheme and invariant differentials
items.statement: A/R is a proper smooth group scheme with geometrically connected fibers; its invariant differentials form the cotangent module at the identity, compatible with base change.
items.note: API: Import A1 and expose evaluation at zero, translation invariance and integral basis. Tests: (1) R may have residue characteristic p; (2) generic and special fibers differ; (3) field-level AbelianVariety does not prove integral freeness.

items.name: Good integral model of a surface in an abelian variety
items.statement: Over the integers R of a finite extension K/Q_p, take an abelian scheme A/R and a closed smooth proper relative surface X/R with geometrically integral fibers, embedded in A.
items.note: API: Expose generic/special fibers, closed immersion, reduction and compatibility under translation and base change. Tests: (1) good reduction of A alone is insufficient for X; (2) special geometric integrality is retained; (3) translation by an R-section preserves the hypotheses.

items.name: Normalized local-field data
items.statement: K/Q_p is finite with ramification index e, residue field k=F_q, q=p^f, and |π|=q⁻¹, hence |p|=p^−[K:Q_p]. On K^n use the maximum norm.
items.note: API: Import local-field carriers, prove normalization conversion and expose open/closed balls. Tests: (1) Q_p gives |p|=p⁻¹; (2) a ramified quadratic field has |p|=q⁻²; (3) open unit ball equals the closed radius-q⁻¹ ball.

items.name: Rank-one subgroup closure
items.statement: For finitely generated G⊂A(K) of rank at most one, Γ is its topological closure; finite torsion and the local identity residue subgroup must be retained.
items.note: API: Construct closure subgroup, reduction image, intersection with the identity disc and translation by Γ. Tests: (1) rank zero means finite G; (2) over K≠Q_p a Z_p-line need not be an R-line; (3) a nonintegral analytic direction is normalized before use.

items.name: Arithmetic and geometric genera
items.statement: For a projective integral curve over an algebraically closed field, p_a=1−χ(O_C) and g is the genus of its normalization. Over a perfect field use geometric base change.
items.note: API: Expose normalization, finite-dimensional coherent cohomology and the distinction between p_a and g. Tests: (1) a smooth curve has p_a=g; (2) a nodal cubic has p_a=1,g=0; (3) a nonsplit node does not become two rational branches.

items.name: Local delta invariant
items.statement: At a point of an integral curve, δ_x is the length/dimension of the finite normalization quotient Õ_C,x/O_C,x, with geometric points used for geometric genus formulas.
items.note: API: Construct normalization algebra, quotient, support and base-change bookkeeping. Tests: (1) smooth point has δ=0; (2) ordinary node has δ=1; (3) cusp has δ=1 but one branch.

items.name: Delta detects regularity
items.statement: For an integral curve over an algebraically closed field, δ_x≥0 and δ_x=0 iff the local ring is regular.

items.name: Normalization genus formula
items.statement: For a projective integral curve over an algebraically closed field, p_a(C)=g(C̃)+Σ_x δ_x.
items.note: G6: original Hironaka source remains to read; main proof uses this exact geometric formula.

items.name: Local curve multiplicity
items.statement: mult_x C is the Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity of the one-dimensional local ring of an integral curve at a closed point.
items.note: API: Expose length-growth definition, invariance under completion, regularity criterion and plane-equation comparison. Tests: (1) smooth point has multiplicity one; (2) ordinary node has multiplicity two; (3) multiplicity is not number of branches.

items.name: Multiplicity-one criterion
items.statement: For an integral curve over an algebraically closed field, mult_x C≥1 with equality iff C is regular at x.

items.name: Multiplicity of a plane local equation
items.statement: If a curve in a surface has local equation F at a regular surface point x, then mult_x C=max{n:F∈m_x^n}.

items.name: Plane singularity delta bound
items.statement: At a regular point of the ambient projective surface, δ_x(C)≥mult_x(C)(mult_x(C)−1)/2.
items.note: G6: Hironaka original proof and characteristic scope remain to acquire.

items.name: Canonical divisor and Chern number
items.statement: On a smooth projective geometrically integral surface S, K_S is the divisor class of det Ω¹ and s=c₁²(S)=K_S²; nef and ample are numerical/geometric conditions, not assumptions on every effective divisor.
items.note: API: Expose divisor of a nonzero two-form, intersection pairing, base change and adjunction. Tests: (1) K² may be zero; (2) an effective divisor need not be ample; (3) abelian surfaces have trivial K.

items.name: Surface adjunction
items.statement: For an integral curve C on a smooth projective surface, 2p_a(C)−2=C²+K_S.C, including singular C.

items.name: Weighted canonical genus bound
items.statement: If D=Σ a_j C_j>0 is a nef canonical divisor on a smooth projective integral surface, with distinct integral components and positive integral multiplicities, then Σa_j(p_a(C_j)−1)≤K_S².

items.name: Formal branches of a curve on a smooth surface
items.statement: After completing at a geometric point of a smooth surface, factor a local curve equation into pairwise nonassociated irreducibles in k[[s₁,s₂]]; the factors define formal branches.
items.note: API: Construct branches independently of coordinates, maps from normalization completions, valuations and multiplicities. Tests: (1) a node has two branches; (2) a cusp has one branch; (3) a globally integral curve can have several formal branches.

items.name: Distinct formal branch factors
items.statement: The completed equation of a reduced integral curve in the smooth-surface setting has no repeated irreducible branch factors.
items.note: Use geometric reducedness/excellence; this is not a statement about arbitrary nonexcellent local domains.

items.name: Branches and normalization fiber
items.statement: Geometric points of the normalization over x correspond to branch ideals in the completed surface local ring.
items.note: Garcia-Fritz Theorem 2.69 proof read; its surrounding thesis is characteristic-zero. The arbitrary-characteristic supplier is still G6.

items.name: Normalization fiber bound
items.statement: For an integral curve on a projective surface regular at x, #ν⁻¹(x)≤mult_x C≤δ_x+1.

items.name: Branch parametrization order bound
items.statement: For irreducible f∈k[[x₁,x₂]] and a parametrization (φ₁,φ₂)∈t k[[t]]² with f(φ₁,φ₂)=0, ord_t φ₁≥ord_x₂ f(0,x₂) and ord_t φ₂≥ord_x₁ f(x₁,0), with zero orders interpreted as ∞.
items.note: G6: obtain Płoski Theorem 2.1 and check nonconstant/zero-coordinate conventions explicitly.

items.name: Surface of general type
items.statement: A smooth projective geometrically integral surface is of general type when its canonical bundle is big, equivalently its pluricanonical section growth is quadratic. Minimal means no smooth rational (−1)-curve.
items.note: API: Expose geometric base change, bigness and minimality without assuming ampleness. Tests: (1) abelian surfaces are excluded; (2) blowing up preserves general type but can destroy nefness; (3) a (−2)-curve can obstruct ampleness.

items.name: Canonical nefness on a minimal general-type surface
items.statement: A minimal smooth projective surface of general type over an algebraically closed field has K nef and K²≥1.
items.note: G6: classification/minimal-surface original proof is not read.

items.name: Canonical ampleness without exceptional rational curves
items.statement: A smooth projective surface of general type containing no smooth rational (−1)- or (−2)-curve has ample K.
items.note: Proof read: minimal nefness, Hodge index, adjunction and Nakai–Moishezon; do not infer ample from nef alone.

items.name: Brody hyperbolic compact complex manifold
items.statement: A compact complex manifold is Brody hyperbolic when every entire map C→M is constant.
items.note: G6: general analytic owner and original Green/Yau/Brody proofs are not yet matched; withheld. API: Expose holomorphic maps, base embedding and the compactness hypothesis for comparison with Kobayashi hyperbolicity. Tests: (1) a point is hyperbolic; (2) an elliptic curve is not; (3) this definition does not itself imply general type.

items.name: Hyperbolic surfaces are of general type
items.statement: A smooth projective complex surface whose analytic manifold is hyperbolic is of general type.
items.note: G6: original analytic/classification input and precise owning stage remain to read; withheld.

items.name: General type of surfaces in abelian varieties
items.statement: A smooth projective complex surface in an abelian variety, not itself a translate of an abelian surface and containing no elliptic curves, is of general type.
items.note: G6: main source offers Yau directly or Green plus Lemma 3.13. Neither original proof acquired; withheld pending owner match.

items.name: Geometric branch count above rational points
items.statement: For a reduced projective curve D/F_q with geometric components C_j and normalizations ν_j, A_D(F_q)=Σ_(x∈D(F_q))Σ_j #ν_j⁻¹(x)(F̄_q).
items.note: API: Expose Frobenius action on components and fibers, weighted versions and extension of constants. Tests: (1) smooth geometrically integral D gives #D(F_q); (2) nonsplit node contributes two geometric branches; (3) A_D need not equal #D̃(F_q).

items.name: Modified curve zeta function
items.statement: Choose a finite extension splitting geometric components and all singular normalization fibers; c_D=Σ_geometric singular x(#ν⁻¹(x)−1). Define Z*_D(T)=Z_D(T)/(1−T)^c_D.
items.note: API: Construct c_D independent of sufficiently large splitting field, rationality and extension norms. Tests: (1) smooth D has c_D=0; (2) a node has c_D=1 regardless of splitting; (3) roots-of-unity norms can cancel zeros and poles.

items.name: Branch count after a splitting extension
items.statement: If L contains a field defining all geometric components and singular normalization points, then A_D(L)=Σ_j #C̃_j(L) and A_D(L)−#D(L)=c_D.

items.name: Roots-of-unity norm identity
items.statement: For splitting degree d, ∏_(ζ^d=1) Z*_D(ζT)=∏_j Z_(C̃_j,F_(q^d))(T^d).
items.note: Identity retained; it does not determine individual poles or zeros because cancellation is possible.

items.name: Unclosed geometric-branch Weil bound
items.statement: The preprint claims A_D(F_q)≤r(q+1)+2√q Σ_j g(C̃_j) for every projective curve with r geometric components.
items.note: G1: false. Over F₃, y²=x²(x−1) is a geometrically integral nodal cubic with nonsplit node, normalization P¹, #C(F₃)=5 and A_C(F₃)=6>4. Withheld, not a theorem target.

items.name: Branch count for a geometrically integral curve with delta correction
items.statement: For a geometrically integral projective curve C/F_q, A_C(F_q)≤#C̃(F_q)+2Σ_geometric x δ_x≤q+1+2g√q+2(p_a−g).
items.locator: Derived repair of Lemma 3.15, restricted scope
items.note: At each rational singular point, only non-F_q-rational branches are extra; their number is zero or at most b≤δ+1≤2δ. Apply Weil to C̃. This does not settle Galois orbits of distinct geometric components in the full weighted surface sum.

items.name: Weil bound on smooth projective curves
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected genus-g curve over F_q, |#C(F_(q^m))−(q^m+1)|≤2g q^(m/2) for every m≥1.

items.name: Global pullback of relative one-forms
items.statement: For f:X→Y over T, define f•:H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y/T)→H⁰(X,Ω¹_X/T) using the adjunction unit and the canonical differential map f*Ω¹_Y/T→Ω¹_X/T.
items.note: API: Expose composition with its canonical pullback isomorphism, identity, restriction to stalks and base change. Tests: (1) identity pulls back identically; (2) constant map over a field pulls back to zero; (3) composition uses the differential map, not just tensor pullback.

items.name: Functoriality of global differential pullback
items.statement: For composable morphisms of T-schemes f,g, (g∘f)•=f•∘g•.
items.note: Garcia-Fritz Proposition 3.29 proof read through its conclusion; EGA universal derivation and adjunction supply the proof.

items.name: Integral morphism for a differential
items.statement: A T-morphism f:X→Y is ω-integral for ω∈H⁰(Y,Ω¹_Y/T) if f•ω=0. Several forms impose simultaneous vanishing.
items.note: API: Expose linearity in ω, composition, base change and affine/stalk criterion. Tests: (1) constant morphisms are integral; (2) in characteristic p Frobenius pulls back all one-forms to zero; (3) vanishing at one tangent vector need not imply integrality of a higher jet.

items.name: Affine and stalk compatibility
items.statement: For a morphism supported at x with affine source, global pullback agrees with the induced map on local-ring Kähler differentials.

items.name: Closed immersed infinitesimal integral arc
items.statement: At x of a smooth surface over k, a length-(m+1) jet is a closed immersion Spec k[z]/(z^(m+1))→S supported at x; require integrality for both specified one-forms.
items.note: API: Expose truncation, support, m=0, closed-immersion criterion and simultaneous pullback. Tests: (1) m=0 is the point; (2) z↦z² alone is not a closed immersed jet; (3) in characteristic p the differential quotient changes when p divides m+1.

items.name: Overdetermined bound for integral jets
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic, let S be a smooth integral surface, ω₁∧ω₂≠0, D=Σa_j C_j its zero divisor and ν_j:C̃_j→S the normalizations. Every closed immersed m-jet through x integral for both forms satisfies m≤Σ_jΣ_(y∈ν_j⁻¹(x)) a_j(ord_y ν_j•ω+1) for every ω∈span_k(ω₁,ω₂), allowing ∞ when ν_j•ω=0.

items.name: Parameters adapted to an immersed jet
items.statement: For m≥1 a closed immersed m-jet into a smooth surface has regular parameters s₁,s₂ such that its completed/local kernel is (s₁^(m+1),s₂); the m=0 point is treated separately.

items.name: Local expression for an integral form
items.statement: In adapted parameters, an integral one-form can be written (G₁s₁^m+G₂s₂) ds₁+G₃ ds₂ with regular local G_i. This is a necessary consequence of the exact truncated differential relation in every characteristic.

items.name: Wedge equation lies in the jet ideal
items.statement: For two integral one-forms as above, their wedge coefficient F belongs to (s₁^m,s₂).

items.name: Zero-length bound away from the wedge divisor
items.statement: If x is outside div(ω₁∧ω₂), every simultaneously integral closed immersed jet has m=0.

items.name: Individual branch order estimate
items.statement: With adapted jet parameters and an irreducible branch equation f, an integral form ω satisfies ord ν•ω≥min(m,ord_s₁ f(s₁,0)−1), with ∞ conventions.

items.name: Printed sharpness example
items.statement: Remark 4.7 proposes ω₁=ds₁+s₁²ds₂, ω₂=ds₁+s₂²ds₂ and the jet (s₁,s₂)=(z,0) in k[z]/z³ as simultaneously integral.
items.note: G2: its pullback is dz≠0 in characteristic ≠2,3. The coordinate must be exchanged; literal claim withheld.

items.name: Corrected sharpness example
items.statement: For char k≠2,3, the same two forms and the closed immersed jet (s₁,s₂)=(0,z) in k[z]/z³ are simultaneously integral and attain the bound m=2.
items.note: The pullbacks are 0 and z²dz=0 because 3 is invertible; the wedge has two transverse branches at the origin.

items.name: Polarization and its isogeny
items.statement: For an ample line bundle H on an n-dimensional abelian variety, φ_H:A→A∨ sends a to t_a*H⊗H⁻¹, with fixed translation convention.
items.note: API: Import the dual variety, tensor law, pullback and Rosati positivity; keep degree of H distinct from degree of φ_H. Tests: (1) principal polarization has degree one; (2) tensor square multiplies φ_H by two; (3) a nonample line bundle need not give an isogeny.

items.name: Degree of a polarization morphism
items.statement: For an ample divisor H on an n-dimensional abelian variety, deg φ_H=(H^n/n!)².

items.name: Polarized cycle and canonical degrees
items.statement: For an r-cycle Z on A, deg_H Z=H^r.Z; for a smooth d-dimensional X⊂A, cdeg_H X=H^(d−1).K_X.
items.note: API: Expose projection formula, translation and numerical equivalence, and distinguish the dimension of Z from ambient n. Tests: (1) for a curve degree is H.C; (2) for a surface canonical degree is H.K_X; (3) abelian subvarieties have canonical degree zero.

items.name: Abelian subvariety generated by a curve
items.statement: After translating a nonempty integral curve to pass through zero, ⟨C⟩ is the smallest abelian subvariety containing it; unpointed statements are understood up to translation.
items.note: API: Construct from its Jacobian map, translation independence for differentials and minimality. Tests: (1) a translated elliptic curve generates an elliptic subvariety after recentering; (2) simple A forces a nonconstant curve to generate A; (3) the raw map ν need not preserve the chosen base point.

items.name: Effective divisors avoiding positive-dimensional translates
items.statement: A nonzero effective divisor on an abelian variety whose support contains no translate of a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety is ample.

items.name: Matsusaka–Morikawa endomorphism
items.statement: For a curve C and divisor H on A, the translate-intersect-sum construction defines α_A(C,H); after a compatible base point it factors as ν_*∘ν*∘φ_H through the Jacobian of C̃.
items.note: API: Prove independence of moving divisor, translation/base-point convention, numerical class and the factorization. Tests: (1) ν(x₀)=0 is needed for ν=ν_*∘j; (2) changing the base point only translates ν; (3) H ample and C generating make α an isogeny.

items.name: Positive trace formula
items.statement: tr α_A(C,H)=2(C.H), with characteristic polynomial det(t−α).
items.note: G3: the proof of CP Lemma 5.4 prints a negative sign for 2Σγ_i. Debarre confirms the positive sign.

items.name: Endomorphism characteristic polynomial
items.statement: For an endomorphism u of an n-dimensional abelian variety, P_u(t)∈Z[t] is the degree-2n polynomial from any ℓ-adic Tate module, ℓ≠char k; P_u(m)=deg([m]−u).
items.note: API: Expose independence of ℓ, integer coefficients, trace and degree including nonisogenies. Tests: (1) u=0 gives t^(2n); (2) u=[m] gives (t−m)^(2n); (3) degree zero is allowed for a nonisogeny.

items.name: Positive roots of the Morikawa polynomial
items.statement: If an integral curve generates polarized A of dimension n, P_α=Q² with monic Q∈Z[t] of degree n and all roots positive real.
items.note: Debarre §2 through Theorem 2.1 and §3 through Lemma 3.6 read. Its Kempf–Mumford–Ramanujan positivity supplier still requires original-source closure.

items.name: Canonical degree of a surface in an abelian threefold
items.statement: For a smooth surface X in an abelian threefold, K_X=X|_X and deg_X X=cdeg_X X=X³=K_X².

items.name: Prime-to-characteristic isogeny is étale
items.statement: An isogeny of abelian varieties of degree prime to char k is étale, so its pullback on invariant differentials is an isomorphism.

items.name: Injectivity of forms on a generating curve
items.statement: Over algebraically closed k of char p, let C generate n-dimensional A and H be ample. If p>n! deg_H(C)^n/(n^n H^n), then H⁰(A,Ω¹)→H⁰(C̃,Ω¹) is injective.
items.note: Proof: α=βφ_H, deg β=M² with positive integer M≤the displayed AM–GM bound; prime-to-p gives injectivity. Correct the trace sign and translate the Abel base point.

items.name: Printed threefold semi-injectivity threshold
items.statement: For X an ample smooth surface in an abelian threefold with no elliptic curves and C a component of an effective canonical divisor, the source claims dim ker(H⁰(A,Ω¹)→H⁰(C̃,Ω¹))≤1 under p>K_X².
items.note: G3: its proof substitutes n=3,H=X incorrectly: the bound is 2(K_X²)²/9, not 2K_X²/3. The weaker printed threshold remains unproved, not disproved; withheld.

items.name: Semi-injectivity under a sufficient threshold
items.statement: In the preceding threefold situation, dim ker≤1 if p>max(s,2s²/9), s=K_X².
items.note: If ⟨C⟩=A use Lemma 5.4 with the corrected threshold; if dim⟨C⟩=2 use adjunction and the canonical genus bound to get p>p_a(C)−1.

items.name: Injectivity on a canonical component in a simple abelian variety
items.statement: If A/k is simple, X⊂A is a smooth surface, D≥0 canonical, C⊂supp D integral, and H ample with p>n! cdeg_H(X)^n/(n^n H^n), then restriction to C̃ is injective.

items.name: Injectivity on a generating surface in a threefold
items.statement: In characteristic p, a smooth generating surface X in an abelian threefold has injective restriction H⁰(A,Ω¹)→H⁰(X,Ω¹).
items.note: G6: this uses Nakai Theorem 5(I); original full proof not acquired, so its supplier remains an explicit design task.

items.name: Injectivity on a surface with a Bertini bound
items.statement: For simple n-dimensional A/k and ample H, restriction to smooth X⊂A is injective if p>3^n n! deg_H(X)^n/(n^n H^n).
items.note: Choose a smooth irreducible curve in |3H|_X; require the actual very-ampleness and Bertini inputs.

items.name: Two-form nonvanishing in an abelian threefold
items.statement: For smooth ample X in an abelian threefold over algebraically closed k of char p, with no elliptic curves, and independent invariant forms ω₁,ω₂, their restrictions have nonzero wedge if p>128(K_X²)²/9.
items.note: This threshold dominates the repaired Lemma 5.5 threshold; retain the quotient-elliptic local valuation argument and Nakai input.

items.name: Two-form nonvanishing in a simple abelian variety
items.statement: For simple A/k of dimension n≥3, smooth surface X, ample H, and independent invariant forms, their restricted wedge is nonzero if p>n!(3deg_H X+cdeg_H X)^n/(n^n H^n).

items.name: Auxiliary curve degree in the wedge argument
items.statement: For a smooth complete intersection curve E=(3H).X, adjunction gives 2g(E)−2=9deg_H X+3cdeg_H X.

items.name: Homogeneous series and directional restriction
items.statement: For H=Σ_α c_α x^α over K, let P_H,m be its homogeneous degree-m part and H_u(z)=H(zu)=Σ_m P_H,m(u)z^m for ||u||=1.
items.note: API: Expose coefficients, substitution, convergence radius and supremum norms. Tests: (1) H_u may vanish identically though H≠0; (2) u is normalized to norm one; (3) degree-zero part must be included in the maximum.

items.name: Zero count and Strassmann index
items.statement: For nonzero h converging on a disc larger than radius r, ν(h,r) is the largest n attaining max |a_n|r^n, and n₀(h,r) counts its zeros in the closed radius-r disc with multiplicity.
items.note: API: Use the built last-maximal-coefficient theorem, expose positivity, scaling and division by a linear factor. Tests: (1) zero series is excluded; (2) constant nonzero series has index zero; (3) zeros on the boundary are included.

items.name: Strassmann zero bound
items.statement: For nonzero h with convergence radius ρ>0 and 0<r<ρ over complete nonarchimedean K, n₀(h,r)≤ν(h,r).

items.name: Directional multivariable zero estimate
items.statement: If |c_α|≤M^(|α|−1), M≥1, ||u||=1, N≥1 and max_(0≤j≤N)|P_H,j(u)|≥1, then ρ_H≥M⁻¹ and for 0<r<M⁻¹, n₀(H_u,r)≤(N−λ)/(1−λ), λ=log M/log(r⁻¹).
items.note: Include M=1 and λ=0, omitted in the proof sentence claiming λ>0.

items.name: Formal coordinates and residue-ball chart
items.statement: For the smooth abelian scheme A/R, parameters at the identity give R[[t₁,…,t_n]] as its completed ring and identify the identity residue disc with m_R^n.
items.note: API: Expose reductions, transition maps, generic fiber and compatibility with the group law. Tests: (1) the chart concerns the identity disc; (2) a model of a nonproper variety has a smaller generic-fiber locus; (3) different coordinates yield a compatible analytic isomorphism.

items.name: Integral parameters adapted to a smooth closed subscheme
items.statement: For a regular closed subscheme X/R through the identity section with smooth relative fibers, parameters for A/R can be chosen so the first codim(X,A) parameters generate the ideal of X near the section.
items.note: Keep the source good-model regularity and relative smoothness, not an arbitrary singular regular-embedding assertion.

items.name: Dimension-n commutative formal group law
items.statement: The completed group law is an n-tuple F(X,Y) over R in 2n variables, F(X,0)=X, F(0,Y)=Y, associative and commutative.
items.note: API: Construct composition, coordinate change, inverse, tangent linearization and multiplication [m]; import the one-dimensional carrier via a comparison. Tests: (1) F=X+Y recovers G_a^n; (2) n=1 multiplicative law recovers G_m; (3) [m] has linear term mX, not order m.

items.name: Normalized formal logarithm and exponential
items.statement: Over the characteristic-zero field K, the completed commutative smooth group has inverse formal maps Log_F and Exp_F with identity linear term, intertwining F and addition. Integral invariant derivations give factorial denominator bounds.
items.note: G4: the printed construction is invalid. A proof route via integral commuting invariant derivations is specified in the report; Bourbaki original must still be checked. API: Construct via commuting invariant derivations or a checked original source; prove inverse/composition identities and uniqueness before analytic evaluation. Tests: (1) additive F gives identity maps; (2) multiplicative F gives log(1+x) and exp(x)−1; (3) multiplication [m] alone is not the finite-difference operator. Continuation (cc-fb70e5): the paper's own series construction is valid once Ψ^[m] is read as the finite difference Δ^m and the logarithm sign is (−1)^{m−1}; see formal-finite-difference-vanishing. Existence of Log/Exp over K is classical for commutative formal groups over Q-algebras (Bourbaki LIE III §5.4, cited by the paper).

items.name: Finite differences of the multiplication maps
items.statement: For a smooth commutative formal group F of dimension n over R, with multiplication series [i](X)∈R[[X]]ⁿ, set Δ^m(X)=Σ_{i=0}^m(−1)^{m−i}C(m,i)[i](X)∈R[[X]]ⁿ. These are the series of Bourbaki III.5.3 that the paper's Ψ^[m] should denote. The paper instead defines Ψ^[m] as [m] (errata E7).
items.note: Added by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5). Integral by construction: an integer combination of the [i]. API: Δ^m as n-tuples of series over R; Δ¹=[1]=Id. Tests: for F=X+Y, Δ¹=X and Δ^m=0 for m≥2; for the multiplicative law in dimension 1, Δ^m=X^m.

items.name: Finite differences vanish below degree m; top-degree identity
items.statement: Over the characteristic-zero fraction field K, let Exp and Log be the normalized formal exponential and logarithm of F, with Exp(x)=Σ_α c_α x^α and Log(X)=Σ_α b_α X^α. For each multi-index α, the coefficient of X^α in [i](X) is a polynomial p_α(i)∈K[i] of degree ≤|α|, whose i^{|α|} coefficient is c_α. Consequently: (a) Δ^m has no terms of degree <m (the corrected Lemma 7.4); (b) the degree-m homogeneous part of Δ^m is m!·(degree-m part of Exp), so Exp(x)=Σ_m(1/m!)·(degree-m part of Δ^m)(x); (c) Log(X)=Σ_{m≥1}((−1)^{m−1}/m)Δ^m(X), converging coefficientwise.
proofSteps: [i](X)=Exp(i·Log X) over K. Expanding, the coefficient of X^α is Σ_{|β|≤|α|}c_β·i^{|β|}·[X^α](Log X)^β, a polynomial in i of degree ≤|α|. Since Log X=X+(higher), [X^α](Log X)^β=δ_{αβ} when |β|=|α|, so the i^{|α|} coefficient is c_α.
The m-th finite difference in i of a polynomial of degree <m is 0, and of a polynomial of degree m with leading coefficient c is m!·c. This gives (a) and (b).

Newton interpolation gives [i]=Σ_m C(i,m)Δ^m coefficientwise, a finite sum in each degree by (a). Differentiating in i at i=0, and using Exp(i Log X)=X+i·Log X+O(i²), gives Log X=Σ_m(d/di C(i,m)|_{i=0})Δ^m=Σ_m((−1)^{m−1}/m)Δ^m. This is (c).

Exact check: for the one-dimensional law with logarithm t+at²+bt³, (b) and (c) reproduce f^{−1} and f through degree 4, while the printed series (with [m] and sign (−1)^m) give 6a²−4b in place of 2a²−b and −f (errata E7).
items.note: Proof supplied by the continuation of Claude Code (cc-fb70e5). Uses only the existence of Log/Exp over a Q-algebra (formal-exp) and polynomial interpolation. This replaces the invariant-derivation route for the factorial bounds; that route remains a valid alternative.

items.name: Linear term of multiplication in a formal group
items.statement: The linear term of the formal multiplication-by-m map is m times the identity.

items.name: Printed vanishing claim for multiplication series
items.statement: The source defines Ψ^[m] as multiplication-by-m and claims that its terms of degree less than m vanish.
items.note: G4: false already for F=X+Y, m=2 over characteristic zero. Withheld.

items.name: Printed logarithm series
items.statement: The preprint writes Log=Σ_(m≥1)(−1)^m Ψ^[m]/m using the multiplication-by-m series, and calls this the formal logarithm.
items.note: G4: wrong linear sign and no coefficientwise convergence under the printed definition. Withheld; finite differences must not be silently substituted as if the source had defined them.

items.name: Factorial and logarithmic denominator bounds
items.statement: For the normalized formal exponential of a smooth commutative formal group over R, each degree-m coefficient c_α satisfies m!c_α∈R. For the normalized logarithm, each degree-M coefficient b_α satisfies |b_α|≤max_{m≤M}|m^{−1}|.
items.note: Proved via finite differences in the cc-fb70e5 continuation. The earlier statement "m·c_α∈R for the logarithm" is not what Lemma 7.5 uses, and is not proved here.
proofSteps: Exponential: by formal-finite-difference-vanishing (b), m!·c_α is a coefficient of Δ^m, which lies in R[[X]]. So m!·c_α∈R for |α|=m.

Logarithm: by (c), the coefficient b_α with |α|=M is Σ_{m≤M}((−1)^{m−1}/m)·(coefficient of X^α in Δ^m), a combination of elements of R with denominators m≤M. So |b_α|≤max_{m≤M}|1/m|, the bound used in Lemma 7.5. The stronger claim M·b_α∈R is not needed for Lemmas 7.5–7.7.

items.name: Formal logarithm convergence
items.statement: Under the preceding corrected logarithm construction, each component of Log_F has convergence radius at least one.
proofSteps: From formal-denominators, |b_α|≤max_{m≤|α|}|1/m|≤|α|^{[K:Q_p]}, which grows at most polynomially in |α|. So the radius of convergence is at least 1 (Lemma 7.5).

items.name: Formal exponential coefficient estimate
items.statement: For a degree-m exponential coefficient with m≥1, |c_α|≤p^([K:Q_p](m−1)/(p−1)); its radius is at least p^−([K:Q_p]/(p−1)).
proofSteps: From formal-denominators, |c_α|≤|1/m!|=p^{[K:Q_p]v_p(m!)}≤p^{[K:Q_p](m−1)/(p−1)}, since v_p(m!)=(m−s_p(m))/(p−1)≤(m−1)/(p−1). The radius bound follows (Lemma 7.6).

items.name: Analytic exponential and logarithm on the identity disc
items.statement: If p>max(e+1,exp(e/exp(1))), Exp_F and Log_F converge as inverse analytic group maps between m_R^n and the identity residue disc, in integral coordinates.
items.note: Requires the corrected formal construction; ordinary real exp appears only in the numerical threshold.

items.name: Logarithm preserves the maximum norm
items.statement: Under the same local-field threshold, |Log_F(t)|=|t| for every t∈m_R^n.

items.name: One-parameter subgroup from a primitive direction
items.statement: For a residue chart t and u∈R^n with ||u||=1, γ(z)=Exp_F(zu), z∈m_R; its image lies in the identity disc.
items.note: API: Expose derivative, injectivity, image subgroup, unit rescaling and coordinate invariance. Tests: (1) u=e₁ gives a coordinate direction; (2) u and a u for a∈R× have the same image; (3) u=0 is excluded.

items.name: Invariant differential hyperplane of a direction
items.statement: H(γ) is the kernel of pullback H⁰(A,Ω¹_A/K)→K dz along γ; evaluation at the primitive tangent vector makes it a codimension-one K-subspace.
items.note: API: Expose evaluation pairing, coordinate-free tangent line, integral lattice and equivalence under unit rescaling. Tests: (1) dimension is n−1; (2) a zero direction would give the whole space; (3) primitive vectors can reduce dependently even if K-independent.

items.name: Pullback along a one-parameter subgroup
items.statement: The pullback of an invariant differential along γ is its value at u times dz; it is surjective onto K dz with kernel H(γ).

items.name: Analytic one-parameter image is a Lie subgroup
items.statement: Under the exponential/logarithm hypotheses, γ identifies the additive group m_R with its image, an analytic one-dimensional Lie subgroup of the identity disc.

items.name: Equivalent primitive directions
items.statement: In fixed coordinates, primitive u,u′ have the same annihilator iff u′=a u for a∈R×.

items.name: Coordinate-independent classification
items.statement: For two one-parameter subgroups, equality of images, equality of annihilator hyperplanes, and intersection containing a nonidentity point are equivalent.

items.name: One-parameter subgroups and hyperplanes
items.statement: Equivalence classes of one-parameter subgroups are in bijection with K-hyperplanes in H⁰(A,Ω¹_A/K).

items.name: A nonidentity local point determines a direction
items.statement: Every nonidentity point of the identity disc lies in a unique one-parameter subgroup image, obtained by normalizing its nonzero logarithm.

items.name: Truncated exponential jets
items.statement: Truncate Exp_F(zu) modulo z^(m+1) to get Spec K[z]/z^(m+1)→A; for m
items.note: API: Expose truncation maps, integral coefficients, reductions and compatibility with completed local rings. Tests: (1) m=0 gives the identity section; (2) m=p can introduce 1/p denominators; (3) a unit linear coefficient gives a closed immersion.

items.name: Integrality of short exponential jets
items.statement: For m

items.name: Closed immersion of exponential jets
items.statement: Every characteristic-zero exponential m-jet is a closed immersion; for m

items.name: Differentials of a characteristic-zero jet
items.statement: For E_m=K[z]/z^(m+1), Ω¹_E_m/K≅(K[z]/z^m)dz.

items.name: Integral differential freeness for short jets
items.statement: For m≤p−2, Ω¹_(R[z]/z^(m+1))/R≅(R[z]/z^m)dz, free over R of rank m, and the analogous formula holds over k. At m=p−1 the relation is p z^(p−1)dz, so freeness fails.

items.name: Continuous differentials of a formal coordinate ring
items.statement: For K[[t₁,…,t_n]], use the completed/universally finite differential module ⊕ K[[t]]dt_i and continuous derivation; construct its map to ordinary differentials of finite jets.
items.note: API: Expose termwise derivative, continuous substitutions, completion comparison and truncation. Tests: (1) ordinary algebraic Ω of K[[t]] is not substituted without proof; (2) finite quotient maps land in ordinary Ω; (3) chain rule agrees on each polynomial.

items.name: Analytic and algebraic differential compatibility
items.statement: For each exponential jet, the analytic pullback of an invariant differential followed by dz↦dz in Ω_E_m/K equals pullback by the algebraic jet.

items.name: Annihilated forms vanish on generic jets
items.statement: Every exponential m-jet is ω-integral for every ω∈H(γ), for all m≥0.

items.name: Integral annihilated forms vanish on reduced short jets
items.statement: If ω∈H(γ) extends over A/R and m≤p−2, its reduction pulls back to zero along the reduced exponential m-jet.
items.note: Use torsion-freeness of integral jet differentials. The larger m

items.name: Source local-field surface bound
items.statement: Assume K/Q_p finite, R its integers, e its ramification index, residue field F_q; A/R an abelian scheme of dimension n≥3 and X/R a smooth proper geometrically integral relative surface closed in A; G⊂A(K) finitely generated of rank≤1 with closure Γ; s=K_X²; p>max(e+1,exp(e/exp(1))); and either (i) n=3, X_K general type, X_F̄q has no elliptic curves, p>128s²/9, or (ii) A_F̄q is simple and an ample H on A_K satisfies p>max(3s+2,n!(3deg_H X+cdeg_H X)^n/(n^n H^n)). The source asserts finiteness and #Γ∩X(K)≤#X(F_q)+(1−e/(p−1))⁻¹(q+4√q+3)s.
items.note: G0/G1/G4/G6: the literal numerical endpoint is withheld pending published-source comparison, a valid weighted branch estimate and closure of cited/formal suppliers.

items.name: Reduction from rank zero to rank one
items.statement: To bound a finite rank-zero subgroup intersection under the local setup, enlarge it by a non-torsion point of the local exponential group; the enlarged finitely generated subgroup has rank one and contains the original.

items.name: Geometry and numerical invariants of good fibers
items.statement: Under the geometric alternatives in Theorem 9.1, both fibers are general type, their canonical self-intersections agree, and the relevant ample intersection degrees agree after specialization.
items.note: G5: in general dimension the top intersection is H^n, not the printed H³. General-type and ampleness proof uses the stated geometric alternatives, not specialization alone.

items.name: No curves of geometric genus zero or one
items.statement: Under the geometric alternatives of Theorem 9.1, every integral geometric curve in the special surface has normalization genus at least two.

items.name: Rank-one closure lies in one analytic subgroup locally
items.statement: Under the local analytic hypotheses, Γ∩U_e is contained in one one-parameter subgroup image.
items.note: Correct the source union symbol to intersection. Over K≠Q_p containment need not be equality with the entire R-line.

items.name: Printed primitive-vector reduction inference
items.statement: The proof of Lemma 9.7 treats two primitive integral, K-linearly independent vectors in the annihilator as independently reducing modulo π.
items.note: G5: false for e₁,e₁+πe₂. The lemma is repaired by choosing a basis of a saturated kernel; this inference is withheld.

items.name: Independent reductions in the annihilator
items.statement: For a primitive u∈R^n, evaluation (R^n)∨→R is split surjective. Its kernel is a free direct summand of rank n−1; when n≥3 select two basis elements whose reductions are independent.
items.note: Extend u to a basis or split by a unit coordinate. The integral invariant differential lattice must first be identified with (R^n)∨.

items.name: Nonzero reduced wedge of annihilating forms
items.statement: Under Theorem 9.1 hypotheses, the two forms furnished by the saturated-kernel construction restrict to u₁,u₂ on the special surface with u₁∧u₂≠0.

items.name: Effective ample canonical divisor of the wedge
items.statement: Under those hypotheses, D=div(u₁∧u₂) is an effective ample canonical divisor defined over F_q; it is nonzero because s>0.

items.name: A form nonzero on every canonical component
items.statement: Under those hypotheses, there is b∈F_p⊂F_q such that ν_j•(u₁+b u₂)≠0 for every geometric component C_j of D.
items.note: Each bad kernel has dimension≤1 and forbids at most one b; #components≤Σa_j≤s<p. Do not choose a different b for each point.

items.name: Maximal simultaneous integral-jet order
items.statement: At x∈X(F̄_q), m(x) is the supremum in N∪{∞} of orders of closed immersed jets integral for u₁,u₂.
items.note: API: Expose existence of the order-zero jet, truncation, upper bounds and translation invariance. Tests: (1) outside D the value is zero; (2) supremum is not assumed finite by definition; (3) the same two forms are used for all jets.

items.name: Vanishing of maximal jet order away from D
items.statement: Under the nonzero-wedge hypothesis, x∉supp D implies m(x)=0.

items.name: Branch formula bounds maximal jet order
items.statement: For the single form w chosen in Lemma 9.10, m(x)≤Σ_jΣ_(y∈ν_j⁻¹(x)) a_j(ord_y ν_j•w+1).

items.name: Uniform finite jet bound
items.statement: Under Theorem 9.1 hypotheses, m(x)≤3Σ_j a_j(p_a(C_j)−1)≤3s<p−2, hence m(x)≤p−3.
items.note: Uses normalization genus, branch≤δ+1, genus-delta and the canonical genus bound, independently of the false finite-field Lemma 3.15.

items.name: Translation to the identity disc
items.statement: For ξ∈Γ∩X(K), translate X by −ξ over R; the geometric hypotheses and m(red ξ) are preserved, and counting its residue-disc intersection reduces to the identity-disc case.
items.note: Retain the leading 1 and ramification factor from Proposition 9.14; the proof display dropping them is a typo.

items.name: A unit coefficient in a defining equation
items.statement: With parameters adapted to X at e and exponential restricted to its primitive direction, some defining parameter has a homogeneous coefficient of absolute value at least one in degree 1≤N≤m(e)+1.
items.note: Otherwise reductions of all equations vanish on a longer short exponential jet, contradicting the definition of m(e). Preserve the bound m≤p−3 needed for reduction of forms.

items.name: Local residue-disc bound
items.statement: Under K/Q_p finite, R its integers, e its ramification index, residue field F_q; A/R an abelian scheme of dimension n≥3 and X/R a smooth proper geometrically integral relative surface closed in A; G⊂A(K) finitely generated of rank≤1 with closure Γ; s=K_X²; p>max(e+1,exp(e/exp(1))); and either (i) n=3, X_K general type, X_F̄q has no elliptic curves, p>128s²/9, or (ii) A_F̄q is simple and an ample H on A_K satisfies p>max(3s+2,n!(3deg_H X+cdeg_H X)^n/(n^n H^n)), for ξ∈Γ∩X(K), x=red ξ, the intersection Γ∩X(K)∩U_x is finite and has at most 1+m(x)/(1−e/(p−1)) points.
items.note: Source-qualified local endpoint: proof uses the repaired formal and saturated-kernel suppliers, but not Lemma 3.15. The unresolved original citations remain G6.

items.name: At most one point away from the canonical divisor
items.statement: Under the local residue bound, any residue disc with reduction outside D has at most one point of Γ∩X(K).

items.name: Global bound retaining the actual jet sum
items.statement: Under the local residue bound, Γ∩X(K) is finite and #Γ∩X(K)≤#X(F_q)+(1−e/(p−1))⁻¹Σ_(x∈X(F_q))m(x).
items.note: Use inequalities in (9.5), not its printed equalities. This endpoint does not assert the q+4√q+3 reduction.

items.name: Unclosed weighted finite-field jet sum
items.statement: The preprint asserts Σ_(x∈X(F_q))m(x)≤(q+4√q+3)s under Theorem 9.1 hypotheses.
items.note: G1: depends on false Lemma 3.15 for components with nonsplit branches or nontrivial Frobenius orbits. The partial geometrically integral correction alone does not close the general weighted sum. Withheld.

items.name: Mordell–Weil for abelian varieties
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a number field F, A(F) is finitely generated.
items.note: The pinned elliptic-curve theorem is insufficient in dimension≥3.

items.name: Source number-field bound
items.statement: For X⊂A over a number field F of Mordell–Weil rank≤1, a finite place v|p with good smooth embedded reduction and satisfying all local hypotheses in Theorem 9.1 over K=F_v, the source asserts #X(F)≤#X(F_q)+(1−e/(p−1))⁻¹(q+4√q+3)K_X².
items.note: G0/G1: global numerical endpoint withheld; Mordell–Weil and injection into X(F_v) explain its conditional reduction.

items.name: Source Q_p specialization
items.statement: For K=Q_p and the geometric alternatives in Theorem 1.1 (the common local contract with e=f=1), the source bound is #Γ∩X(Q_p)≤#X(F_p)+(p−1)/(p−2)(p+4√p+3)s.
items.note: G0/G1: withheld numerical endpoint; threshold on p forces the analytic hypotheses.

items.name: Source rational bound in a threefold
items.statement: For smooth geometrically integral general-type X⊂A/Q with dim A=3, rank A(Q)≤1, good reduction at p>128s²/9 and no elliptic curve in X_F̄p, the source claims #X(Q)≤#X(F_p)+(p−1)/(p−2)(p+4√p+3)s.
items.note: G0/G1: withheld numerical endpoint.

items.name: Source rational bound in arbitrary ambient dimension
items.statement: For smooth geometrically integral X⊂A/Q, dim A=n≥3, rank A(Q)≤1, good reduction at p, A_F̄p simple and ample H with p>max(3s+2,n!(3deg_H X+cdeg_H X)^n/(n^n H^n)), the source claims the same Q-bound.
items.note: G0/G1: withheld numerical endpoint.

items.name: Density-one geometrically simple reductions
items.statement: For A/Q of odd dimension with End(A_C)=Z, good primes with geometrically simple reduction have density one.
items.note: G6: original source, density convention, monodromy hypotheses and atlas supplier not read; withheld rather than deriving this merely from End=Z.

items.name: Source density-one surface-bound application
items.statement: For an abelian threefold A/Q with rank≤1 and End(A_C)=Z, there is a density-one set of good primes such that every smooth geometrically integral surface X/Q in A and p in that set, good for X with p>128(K_X²)²/9, satisfies the source rational bound.
items.note: G0/G1/G6: withheld. The density-one set is chosen from A; it is not asserted that one prime works uniformly for all surface degrees.

items.name: Symmetric square and Abel map
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve C, C^(2) parametrizes effective degree-two divisors; with a chosen degree-two divisor d₀ over the base, j(D)=[D−d₀] maps to J=Pic⁰(C).
items.note: API: Import the symmetric-power and Picard/Abel construction from JC; expose image W₂, diagonal and point-divisor curves. Tests: (1) a quadratic closed point defines a rational symmetric-square point; (2) a pair of conjugates is not two rational points; (3) absence of a rational effective degree-two divisor makes C^(2)(F) empty.

items.name: Point and diagonal divisor classes on C^(2)
items.statement: For char k≠2, V is the numerical class of x+C and Δ is the image of the diagonal C→C²→C^(2); θ=j*Θ is the theta class.
items.note: API: Expose finite quotient pullbacks, degree-two ramification, numerical equivalence and Abel base-point independence. Tests: (1) pullback of V is the sum of the two point fibers; (2) diagonal pullback carries multiplicity two; (3) θ can be nef without ample on hyperelliptic C^(2).

items.name: Symmetric-square basic intersection numbers
items.statement: For genus-g C over algebraically closed k with char k≠2, V²=1, Δ.V=2 and Δ²=4−4g.

items.name: Canonical class and square on C^(2)
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, K_(C^(2))≡(2g−2)V−Δ/2 and K²=(4g−9)(g−1).

items.name: Printed canonical ampleness for every genus≥3 curve
items.statement: The source claims that C^(2) has ample canonical divisor for every curve of genus g≥3.
items.note: G5: false for hyperelliptic genus three: the contracted g¹₂ curve E≃P¹ has θ.E=K.E=0. Withheld.

items.name: Canonical ampleness for nonhyperelliptic symmetric squares
items.statement: For a nonhyperelliptic smooth projective curve of genus g≥3 over algebraically closed k, char k≠2, C^(2) has ample canonical divisor.
items.note: j is a closed immersion so θ is ample; V is nef via its moving family, giving ample+nef. Ample plus arbitrary effective is not a valid argument.

items.name: Theta canonical intersection
items.statement: For C of genus g≥3 in the same setting, θ.K_(C^(2))=2g(g−2).

items.name: Closed immersion of the nonhyperelliptic Abel square
items.statement: For nonhyperelliptic C of genus≥3, j:C^(2)→J is a closed immersion identifying C^(2) with W₂, with the scheme and tangent argument required.
items.note: Pointwise injectivity by absence of g¹₂ is not alone sufficient to prove closed immersion; include the Abel differential/linear-system criterion from JC suppliers.

items.name: Descent of twice the theta class
items.statement: If C/F has an effective F-rational divisor d₀=x₁+x₂ of degree two, the sum of the two associated theta translates is an F-defined ample divisor H on J with H≡2Θ.

items.name: Polarization degrees for W₂
items.statement: With H≡2Θ and nonhyperelliptic C of genus g≥3, H^g=2^g g!, H².W₂=4g(g−1), and H.K_W₂=4g(g−2).
items.note: Poincaré cycle formula original input remains G6; retain scheme identification C^(2)≃W₂.

items.name: Symmetric-square prime threshold
items.statement: The arbitrary-dimensional geometric threshold specializes to (8g−10)^g, which exceeds 3(4g−9)(g−1)+2 for g≥3.

items.name: Source symmetric-square rational-point bound
items.statement: For geometrically nonhyperelliptic C/Q of genus g≥3 with rank J(Q)≤1, good p>(8g−10)^g, geometrically nonhyperelliptic reduction and geometrically simple J_Fp, the source asserts #C^(2)(Q)≤#C_Fp^(2)(F_p)+(p−1)/(p−2)(p+4√p+3)(4g−9)(g−1).
items.note: G0/G1: numerical endpoint withheld.

items.name: Genus-three numerical threshold
items.statement: For a nonhyperelliptic genus-three curve, K_(C^(2))²=6, 128·6²/9=512, and the least prime exceeding this threshold is 521.

items.name: Source genus-three quadratic-point bound
items.statement: For geometrically nonhyperelliptic genus-three C/Q with rank J(Q)≤1, good p≥521, geometrically nonhyperelliptic C_Fp and no elliptic curve in C_F̄p^(2), the source asserts #C^(2)(Q)≤#C_Fp^(2)(F_p)+6(p−1)/(p−2)(p+4√p+3)<#C_Fp^(2)(F_p)+7.1p.
items.note: G0/G1: withheld. Balakrishnan–Caro 2025 introduction quotes published CP Corollary 1.15 with +5 and for W₂, demonstrating that v2 is not a final-version substitute.

items.name: Smooth surface Weil point-count estimate
items.statement: For smooth projective geometrically connected X/F_p of dimension two, |#X(F_p)−(p²+1)|≤b₁√p+b₂p+b₃p^(3/2), with b_i geometric ℓ-adic Betti numbers.
items.note: Comparison with complex Betti numbers requires a lift and the proper smooth comparison; an arbitrary Q_p variety is not supplied a canonical complex embedding.

prerequisites.why: G0: acquire the 54-page publication and compare it with the fully read 39-page arXiv v2. Publisher PDF URL returned HTML; no final matching is claimed.

prerequisites.citation: Debarre, Degrees of curves in abelian varieties, Bull. SMF 122 (1994), 343–361
prerequisites.why: Selected §2 through Theorem 2.1 and §3 through Lemma 3.6, plus beginning of §4, read. Supplies positive roots, degree and positive trace; acquire the original Kempf–Mumford–Ramanujan/Matsusaka/Morikawa suppliers for full closure.

prerequisites.citation: Garcia-Fritz, Curves of low genus on surfaces and applications to Diophantine problems, thesis (2015)
prerequisites.why: Selected Theorem 2.69 and proof, §3.1 integrality definition, and §3.2 Proposition 3.29 and its proof read. General scheme pullback is usable; the surrounding branch theory assumes characteristic zero and does not itself close the arbitrary-characteristic branch input.

Exact bibliography and resume locators appear in the report. They are explicit source tasks, not checked black boxes.

routes.reason: Relative invariant differentials are already A1 targets; import the built field carrier.
Polarization and ample-divisor criteria belong to the canonical dual/polarization owner.
Degree-prime-to-p étaleness is an isogeny supplier, not a surface-specific axiom.
Tate characteristic polynomials, Rosati positivity and Morikawa degree/trace comparisons extend the stated endomorphism-degree scope.
Use the birational and single Chow/intersection owners for minimality, adjunction, Hodge index, positivity and canonical numerical estimates.

The existing birational stage explicitly needs curve normalization; supply finite normalization, branches, delta and their comparison here. Import the smooth curve/JC dictionaries from SF.3 instead of replanning upstream.
Good embedded models specialize the existing DVR-model and deformation supplier; the relative abelian group is imported from A1.
Reuse the built ring differential carrier and sheaf-module infrastructure; add the actual relative differential sheaf, its pullback and finite-jet computations.
Zeta extension arithmetic and point-count inequalities retain the Weil owner; the false branch bound is explicitly excluded.
ED.4 explicitly owns Strassmann/Newton zero bounds; route the abstract directional estimate there for reuse by its surface successor.
AdicEtaleGeometry A2 explicitly names AdicSpacesPartII as canonical geometric owner; formal charts and continuous differential comparisons go here, not to a second analytic carrier.
General Mordell–Weil is the existing descent/height target; the elliptic theorem is imported only as a special case.

routes.title: Abelian schemes and arithmetic moduli, Part II: integral formal Lie theory
routes.reason: A1 supplies invariant differentials but has no dimension-general formal logarithm, integral exponential or short-jet comparison. The built FormalGroup is one-dimensional, and elliptic formal groups are already upstream; this is their higher-dimensional successor.
routes.brief: Import Abelian Schemes and Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A1, Adic Spaces Part II (AdicSpacesPartII) F0/R1/R2, the built scalar analytic differentiation API and formal power series, tangent spaces and one-dimensional FormalGroup. Construct n-dimensional commutative formal laws on the existing series carrier, invariant integral derivations/forms, normalized formal Exp/Log, factorial/logarithmic denominator estimates, coordinate changes and convergence. Use commuting derivations D^α(t_j)(0)/α! and homogeneous integration of closed invariant forms, or acquire and verify Bourbaki III §5; the printed CP multiplication-series argument is invalid and is not an axiom. For finite K/Q_p with |π|=q⁻¹ and p>max(e+1,exp(e/exp(1))), prove inverse analytic Exp/Log on m_R^n, norm preservation, classification of one-parameter images by invariant-form hyperplanes, and short jets. Final interface: for primitive u and m

routes.title: Effective Diophantine methods, Part II: surface Chabauty and quadratic points
routes.reason: ED.4 treats curves; surfaces require simultaneous integral jets, geometric nonvanishing and a rank-one formal direction. These are new layers in the same direction, not nonabelian Chabauty or a new rational-point programme.
routes.brief: Import Effective Diophantine Methods (EffectiveDiophantineMethods) ED.4 for zero bounds; Abelian Schemes and Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A1–A4/A6 and its proposed Formal Lie Theory Part II; Scheme and Stack Foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.0/4/5; Jacobian Challenge (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge) C/D/F; Weil Conjectures (WeilConjectures) WC.1/5; and Heights, Rational Points and Obstructions (HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions) RP.1. Prove CP Theorem 4.4 exactly as item overdetermined, in arbitrary characteristic, with closed immersed jets, geometric branches and infinite-order conventions. Develop Morikawa-based curve restriction, surface one-form injectivity and Lemma 5.7 two-form nonvanishing; correct Lemma 5.5(i) to the sufficient p>max(s,2s²/9). Close original Nakai, positivity, singularity and general-type suppliers rather than assume them. For the exact common local hypotheses recorded in main-local-source, construct two independently reducing annihilating forms using a saturated kernel, D=div(u₁∧u₂), one global combination nonzero on every component and m(x)≤3s≤p−3. First final target is Proposition 9.14: #Γ∩X(K)∩U_x≤1+m(x)/(1−e/(p−1)); summation gives the explicit finite jet-sum bound. The historical preprint target is #Γ∩X(K)≤#X(F_q)+(1−e/(p−1))⁻¹(q+4√q+3)s, but this is a BLOCKED source endpoint: Lemma 3.15 is false and the 54-page publication must be acquired and matched before this or its Q/number-field/symmetric-square corollaries becomes an accepted theorem target. Do not silently replace +3 by the +5 quoted in Balakrishnan–Caro. The present route excludes those endpoint items. For nonhyperelliptic C, construct C^(2)≃W₂, its canonical and theta intersections, descent of H≡2Θ and thresholds (8g−10)^g and p≥521 in genus three. Hyperelliptic genus-three C^(2) has nonample K and cannot be imported as an ample example. Keep density-one simple reduction and hyperbolicity originals as explicit unclosed G6 inputs. Give consumer-derived APIs and ≥3 tests per definition, including nonsplit nodes, ramification and boundary jets; no Lean implementation is claimed.
